content: 1. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the quadrivalent intranasal influenza virus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Before initiating ustekinumab therapy, patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations as per current guidelines. Immunosuppressants, including ustekinumab, increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 2. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the recombinant quadrivalent influenza virus vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should complete all recommended immunizations prior to starting ustekinumab therapy. Immunosuppressants also heighten the risk of infection with live vaccines. 3. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the trivalent influenza virus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before starting ustekinumab therapy. Immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 4. Ustekinumab diminishes the effects of the adjuvanted trivalent influenza virus vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should complete all recommended immunizations before initiating ustekinumab therapy. Immunosuppressants elevate the risk of infection with live vaccines. 5. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the live measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before starting ustekinumab therapy. Immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 6. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the live measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella (MMRV) vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 7. Ustekinumab and irinotecan may interact due to altered CYP450 enzyme activity caused by chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving irinotecan. 8. Ustekinumab and isavuconazonium sulfate both reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should complete all age-appropriate immunizations before starting ustekinumab therapy. Immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 10. Ustekinumab and leflunomide both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Ustekinumab and levothyroxine may interact due to altered CYP450 enzyme activity caused by chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving levothyroxine. 12. Ustekinumab and lisocabtagene maraleucel both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Ustekinumab and lithium may interact due to altered CYP450 enzyme activity caused by chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving lithium. 14. Ustekinumab and lomustine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the pneumococcal 13-valent vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 16. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the polyvalent pneumococcal vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 17. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the inactivated poliovirus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible, as antibody responses may be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence is restored. 18. Ustekinumab and prazosin may interact due to altered CYP450 enzyme activity caused by chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving prazosin. 19. Ustekinumab and primidone may interact due to altered CYP450 enzyme activity caused by chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving primidone. 20. Ustekinumab and procainamide may interact due to altered CYP450 enzyme activity caused by chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving procainamide. 21. Ustekinumab and quinidine may interact due to altered CYP450 enzyme activity caused by chronic inflammation. Monitor closely for therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving quinidine. 22. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the rabies vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 23. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the chick embryo cell-derived rabies vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 24. Ustekinumab and rilonacept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the live oral rotavirus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should complete all age-appropriate immunizations before starting ustekinumab therapy. Immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 26. Ustekinumab and rozanolixizumab may interact, potentially reducing ustekinumab levels or effects. Monitor closely.
